Article Title: From Anaya Bangar’s cricket return to Imane Khelif’s Olympic gold controversy: The biggest transgender and gender-eligibility debates in sport
Article Text:
The biggest transgender and gender-eligibility debates in sport (Agency Images)

Anaya Bangar returns to cricket

Laurel Hubbard: the Olympic milestone

Lia Thomas and the battle that changed American college sport

Emily Bridges and the battle over cycling

Emily Bridges. (Twitter Photo)

Imane Khelif: The boxing controversy that blurred the lines

Imane Khelif (Image Via Getty)

The WNBA debate too

NEW DELHI: Anaya Bangar's return to cricket has opened a much bigger conversation about transgender athletes in sport, one that now extends far beyond the cricket field.The former Mumbai Under-19 cricketer has received clearance from Cricket Australia to play women's community cricket in the country, giving her a route back into competitive cricket after beginning her transition in 2022. Bangar can participate in Premier Cricket, which Cricket Australia classifies as community cricket, immediately. Her pathway to elite cricket from March 2027, however, comes with eligibility conditions, including a requirement to provide a blood test confirming that her serum testosterone remains below the prescribed threshold and that she continues to meet the governing body's policy requirements.The decision has already divided opinion. South Africa all-rounder Marizanne Kapp publicly criticised Cricket Australia's position, describing the decision as "absolutely ridiculous" and arguing against transgender women competing in women's cricket.Bangar's case is therefore not simply about one cricketer. The Olympics have taken a very different routeFew athletes illustrate that change more clearly than New Zealand weightlifter Laurel Hubbard.Hubbard became the first openly transgender woman to compete at an Olympic Games when she took part in the women's super-heavyweight weightlifting competition at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021. She did not complete a successful lift in the competition and finished without a result.At the time, her participation was viewed as a landmark moment for transgender representation in elite sport.Five years later, the IOC has adopted a fundamentally different approach. From Los Angeles 2028, transgender women who do not satisfy the IOC's biological-sex eligibility requirements will not be eligible for the women's category at the Games.In the United States, swimmer Lia Thomas became one of the most prominent figures in the debate. Thomas competed for the University of Pennsylvania after transitioning and became the first openly transgender athlete to win an NCAA Division I individual title when she won the women's 500-yard freestyle in 2022.Her participation triggered intense debate over eligibility, fairness and the rules governing transgender athletes in collegiate sport.The issue has since moved well beyond one swimmer. In June 2026, the US Supreme Court ruled that laws in West Virginia and Idaho restricting transgender athletes from participating on female school and college teams did not violate Title IX. The court's decision cleared the way for states to maintain such restrictions based on biological sex.Cycling produced another highly visible case through British rider Emily Bridges. Bridges, who had previously competed in men's cycling, sought to compete in women's events after transitioning. Her eligibility became the subject of intense debate in 2022 when she was ruled ineligible for the women's event at the British National Omnium Championships.The wider issue eventually contributed to a significant change in international cycling policy. The Union Cycliste Internationale, cycling's world governing body, changed its rules in 2023 and prohibited transgender women who transitioned after male puberty from competing in women's events on its international calendar. The organisation said its decision was based on the available scientific evidence and the need to protect equal opportunities in the women's category.The transgender debate in sport is also frequently linked to another high-profile case, but Imane Khelif's story needs to be treated separately.Khelif is not a transgender athlete. The Algerian boxer was born and raised as a woman and competed in the women's 66kg category at the Paris 2024 Olympics, where she went on to win the gold medal.Yet her participation became one of the biggest controversies of the Games.The issue stemmed from a dispute between boxing's governing bodies. The International Boxing Association (IBA) said Khelif had failed its eligibility requirements at the 2023 World Championships and claimed that testing had found her ineligible to compete in the women's category. However, the IBA did not publicly release the underlying test results. The IOC, which was responsible for the boxing competition at Paris 2024, rejected the IBA's position and allowed Khelif to compete.The conversation has also reached women's basketball in the United States. Indiana Fever player Sophie Cunningham recently reignited the debate after speaking publicly about transgender participation in women's sport. Her comments generated both support and criticism, forcing the WNBA to address an issue that had largely remained outside the league's immediate competitive spotlight.WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert subsequently told teams that the league would continue discussing transgender participation, acknowledging the growing attention surrounding the issue.The situation is particularly interesting because there is currently no openly transgender player competing in the WNBA.
Article Summary: Anaya Bangar's return to cricket has opened a much bigger conversation about transgender athletes in sport. The former Mumbai Under-19 cricketer has received clearance from Cricket Australia to play women's community cricket in the country. Bangar can participate in Premier Cricket, which Cricket Australia classifies as community cricket, immediately. Her pathway to elite cricket from March 2027 comes with eligibility conditions.

Article Title: Chungreng Koren falls to Ryo Tajima in Road to UFC semifinal
Article Text:
Chungreng Koren

NEW DELHI: Chungreng Koren’s Road to UFC Season 5 campaign came to an end on Friday as the Indian fighter suffered a unanimous decision loss to Japan’s Ryo Tajima in their bantamweight semifinal in Shanghai.Koren, who had entered the semifinal after submitting Japan’s previously unbeaten Ryuho Miyaguchi in the quarterfinals, was unable to turn his grappling control into enough effective offence throughout the 15-minute contest.The Indian started aggressively, using leg kicks before taking the fight towards the cage. Koren eventually secured a takedown and looked to establish control.Tajima, however, quickly worked his way back to his feet and briefly managed to take Koren’s back.In the second round, even though Koren repeatedly looked to put Tajima against the cage, the Japanese continued to find opportunities to score with short punches. He also connected with a right hand during the round.Koren continued to press forward in the third round and again took Tajima down. He spent long stretches controlling the Japanese fighter on the mat and finished the contest with more than eight minutes of control time.Tajima, though, continued to work whenever he found an opening. He landed short punches and knees during the exchanges, and those moments ultimately proved important as the fight went to the judges.The scorecards were 30-27, 29-28 and 29-28, all in favour of Tajima.The defeat ends Koren’s run in the tournament and leaves him short of the Road to UFC final, where a tournament victory would have earned a UFC contract.The loss also brings an end to what had been a significant second chance for the Manipuri fighter.Koren had entered the tournament’s opening round in May on short notice after initially being named as a backup. He had struggled to make the bantamweight limit before facing Miyaguchi in Macau but produced an impressive comeback inside the cage, dropping his opponent with a left hand before securing a rear-naked choke in the second round.Ahead of the semifinal, Koren had spoken about how different his preparation was this time. He had spent three months at home, returned to training after a short break and also worked in Phuket with UFC fighters and other high-level training partners.The 27-year-old had also spoken openly about the difficult period that followed his loss to Rabindra Dhant in 2025. That defeat had left him struggling with his discipline and physical condition, forcing him to rebuild his routine before getting another opportunity on the Road to UFC.This time, he made weight and entered the fight with a full camp behind him.But Tajima proved difficult to break down.For Koren, the result means another UFC opportunity has slipped away. Yet his Road to UFC run had already marked a significant step forward after his first opportunity to enter the tournament fell through.
Article Summary: Chungreng Koren loses to Japan's Ryo Tajima in bantamweight semifinal. Defeat ends Koren’s run in the tournament and leaves him short of the Road to UFC final. Defeat also brings an end to what had been a significant second chance for Koren.

Article Title: ‘Go and educate yourself’: Anaya Bangar hits back at Marizanne Kapp over cricket return
Article Text:
Anaya Bangar hits back at Marizanne Kapp

Anaya responds to Kapp criticism

‘Baby steps from here’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Anaya Bangar has responded to criticism from South Africa all-rounder Marizanne Kapp over her bid to return to competitive women’s cricket, urging those opposed to her participation to “educate themselves” on the subject. Kapp had strongly criticised Cricket Australia’s decision to offer Anaya a pathway back into competitive women’s cricket , calling it “absolutely ridiculous” and saying “this should not be allowed”.The comments came after Cricket Australia cleared Anaya, daughter of former India cricketer and coach Sanjay Bangar, for a pathway towards elite women’s cricket under its Inclusion of Transgender and Gender Diverse Players in Elite Cricket Policy.Anaya, who underwent gender-affirming surgery in March this year, is currently eligible to play community cricket in any state or territory of Australia. Her eligibility for elite cricket from March 2027 remains subject to the policy requirements.Anaya’s potential return has generated reactions on both sides, with the 25-year-old now responding directly to Kapp’s criticism.“I think people who want to raise their voice against it should actually educate themselves on this topic, and I've already provided the necessary information in terms of not having any unfair advantage, and also complying with the guidelines set by Cricket Australia.“If anyone's personal opinion is in that sort of way, I hope they go and educate themselves,” she said with a shrug while speaking to PTI.Anaya is hoping to eventually pursue a pathway to the Women’s Big Bash League, although she is yet to sign up with a local club. Her immediate focus is on playing at the community level and proving herself through her performances.Anaya said she had spent a long period in “survival mode” and was only now beginning to process everything she had experienced during her transition and the long road back to cricket.“...basically now, the next role is to go there and play club cricket and prove myself by my performances, and if I do well, I hopefully might have a chance to be picked for the Women's Big Bash League. So, baby steps from here, but the major part of having a place to play has been cleared,” she said.She is currently in talks with a few cricket clubs and is waiting to decide on the right one “to go there and start playing.”For Anaya, the CA decision represents a significant breakthrough after years away from competitive cricket. While she has been given a pathway, it does not guarantee selection in any team.Anaya further added that the process was neither “automatic or informal”, with CA considering her medical and surgical history, hormone and testosterone levels, cricketing background, playing footage and scientific and athletic performance work undertaken with Manchester Metropolitan University’s Institute of Sport.She also said her most recent blood test in July recorded total testosterone at 0.6 nanomoles, which she said was within the female reference range reported by the laboratory.
Article Summary: Anaya Bangar has responded to criticism from South Africa all-rounder Marizanne Kapp over her bid to return to competitive women’s cricket. Cricket Australia cleared Anaya, daughter of former India cricketer and coach Sanjay Bangar, for a pathway towards elite women's cricket under its Inclusion of Transgender and Gender Diverse Players in Elite Cricket Policy. Anaya underwent gender-affirming surgery in March.

Article Title: 'Test cricket needs character': Gautam Gambhir's message after India's draw against Sri Lanka in Colombo
Article Text:
Gautam Gambhir

Gambhir praises India, singles out Dinusha

Padikkal, Jurel power India to 503

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

112-run stand changes the game

Poll Vote & Share your view Who stood out the most for Sri Lanka in the Test series? Sonal Dinusha Asitha Fernando Pasindu Sooriyabandara 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

India head coach Gautam Gambhir praised his team for displaying the character and mental strength required in Test cricket after Shubman Gill ’s side secured a 1-0 series victory over Sri Lanka. India had a chance to complete a 2-0 sweep after winning the series opener in Galle, but Sri Lanka mounted a spirited fightback in Colombo to force a draw despite being asked to follow on.Following the conclusion of the series, Gambhir took to social media to acknowledge India's performance while also highlighting the impact of Sri Lanka batter Sonal Dinusha."Test cricket needs character, patience and mental toughness that's shown by our boys! Special shoutout to Sonal Dinusha for his exceptional performance," Gambhir wrote on X.Dinusha was the central figure in Sri Lanka's resistance. He scored centuries in both innings of the Colombo Test, including an unbeaten 133 in the second innings, frustrating India's efforts to wrap up the match.India made a dominant start after choosing to bat first in Colombo. Devdutt Padikkal led the charge with a superb 117, while Dhruv Jurel remained unbeaten on 115. Rishabh Pant added 63 and captain Gill contributed 50 as India amassed 503/9 before declaring. Asitha Fernando was Sri Lanka's most successful bowler, finishing with four wickets.Sri Lanka were dismissed for 290 in their first innings, but Dinusha once again stood out with a composed 103.Pasindu Sooriyabandara also played an important role, scoring 80, while India's Prasidh Krishna and Manav Suthar claimed three wickets each. Asked to follow on, Sri Lanka were in serious trouble at 218/6 and India appeared to be closing in on another victory. Dinusha, however, refused to give India an opening.Dinusha joined forces with Keshara Nuwantha to produce a crucial 112-run partnership. Nuwantha's 46 came from 150 deliveries as the pair absorbed pressure and consumed valuable overs. Sri Lanka's lower order then provided further support, allowing Dinusha to remain at the crease until the close.He finished unbeaten on 133 from 264 balls, with eight fours and two sixes, as Sri Lanka reached 429/9 to secure the draw. The result ended India's hopes of a clean sweep but secured them a 1-0 series victory.India had established their series advantage in the opening Test at Galle, where they secured a 165-run victory. Manav Suthar was the star of the contest, claiming his maiden 10-wicket haul in Test cricket, while Padikkal played a pivotal role with a 167 in India's first innings.
Article Summary: Gautam Gambhir praises India, singles out Sonal Dinusha. India secured 1-0 series victory over Sri Lanka. India had a chance to complete a 2-0 sweep after winning the series opener in Galle. Sri Lanka mounted a spirited fightback in Colombo to force a draw.

Article Title: ‘Treated with the dignity anyone deserves’: Pat Cummins backs campaign for Imran Khan
Article Text:
Pat Cummins and Imran Khan

Former captains seek medical care, family access

Chappell raises concerns over Khan’s health

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Australia captain Pat Cummins has thrown his support behind a campaign led by former international cricket captains seeking proper medical care and family access for jailed Pakistan great Imran Khan , saying the former all-rounder should be treated with “the dignity anyone deserves”.Cummins, one of the leading active cricketers in world cricket, backed the appeal on Friday after former Australia captain Greg Chappell and 20 other ex-international captains called for Khan to receive humane treatment and independent medical care.“Adding my support here to GC (Greg Chappell) and the other former international captains. I hope the court ordered medical assessment be allowed to run its course, and that family visits continue.“I hope Imran Khan is treated with the dignity anyone deserves,” Cummins posted on X, quoting a short clip of Chappell expressing concerns about Khan’s wellbeing.The intervention makes Cummins one of the first active international cricketers to publicly speak out in support of the campaign surrounding Khan’s medical care.Khan, 73, has been in custody in Rawalpindi since 2023 after being convicted on corruption charges.He recently underwent a medical examination in Islamabad before being returned to prison.His sons, Sulaiman and Kasim, have expressed fears over their father's safety and claimed that attempts are being made to kill him. Cummins echoed the former captains’ call for Khan’s family to continue having access to him.The petition, led by Chappell and addressed to Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, has been signed by 21 former international captains, including India greats Sunil Gavaskar , Kapil Dev and Dilip Vengsarkar, as well as Sir Alastair Cook, Michael Atherton, Steve Waugh, Adam Gilchrist and Nasser Hussain.The signatories called for a comprehensive health evaluation by a Supreme Court-directed medical board that includes Khan’s personal physicians, uninterrupted weekly family visits and immediate implementation of any recommended treatment.“Imran Khan is 73 years old and has now spent more than three years in custody. Whatever the legal and political arguments surrounding his case, the basic decency of ensuring a court-ordered medical process is actually completed is not, in our view, a controversial request,” the letter stated.The former captains described themselves as “former colleagues and rivals who share a bond forged on the cricket field” and argued that this bond “transcends the borders and disputes that too often divide countries”.Chappell had previously spoken about his concerns during an appearance on The Grade Cricketer podcast, recalling meeting Khan in Pakistan six years ago and describing him then as a “strong, robust older man”.“That’s not the case anymore. His right eye apparently has developed a disability… he’s struggling. He’s been in isolation for three years,” Chappell said.He also described seeing a recent video in which Khan was reportedly taken to hospital in a wheelchair.“He didn’t look well at all. He didn’t look robust. He didn’t look like he could really get around very much,” Chappell said.The former Australia captain also expressed concern about Khan’s reported isolation and its potential impact on his mental and physical health.Khan remains an iconic figure in Pakistan cricket history, having captained the country to its maiden ODI World Cup title in 1992. He later served as Pakistan’s prime minister from 2018 to 2022.Khan has denied wrongdoing and described the cases against him as politically motivated.
Article Summary: Former captains seek medical care, family access for jailed Imran Khan. Australia captain Pat Cummins has thrown his support behind the campaign. Former Australia captain Greg Chappell and 20 other ex-international captains called for Khan to receive humane treatment and independent medical care.

Article Title: FIFA World Cup’s most-hated hydration breaks could be ‘soft-launched’ in the Champions League
Article Text:
Ben Foster fears World Cup hydration breaks could eventually be trialled in the Champions League/ Image: AP

not

Why hydration breaks caused such a stir

Portugal players cool down during a hydration break during the World Cup Group K soccer match between Colombia and Portugal in Miami Gardens, Fla., Saturday, June 27, 2026. (AP Photo/Lynne Sladky)

Foster fears football is becoming ‘quarters’

Why Foster thinks the Champions League could be next

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

One of the most controversial features introduced at the 2026 World Cup could have a life beyond the tournament, with former England goalkeeper Ben Foster fearing that what began as a tournament measure could eventually become part of the regular club football landscape.Hydration breaks proved hugely unpopular with sections of supporters during the World Cup, with the three-minute stoppages midway through each half disrupting the flow of matches and prompting questions over whether football was becoming too fragmented. Foster now believes the Premier League and Champions League could eventually face the same change, although the Premier League has confirmed that it willintroduce mandatory, blanket hydration breaks among its rule changes for the 2026-27 season.FIFA introduced mandatory three-minute hydration breaks midway through each half at the World Cup, meaning matches were effectively divided into four separate periods rather than two continuous 45-minute halves.The interruptions were criticised by players and managers who felt they affected the momentum and identity of matches, with USMNT head coach Mauricio Pochettino making his position clear during the tournament."I don’t like it. I only like it when the conditions are extreme. But when the conditions are good, it is unnecessary," Pochettino said.The commercial side of the decision also attracted attention because broadcasters could use the stoppages as advertising opportunities. A 30-second World Cup commercial slot on Fox Sports reportedly cost between $200,000 and $300,000, with prices reaching around $750,000 during the latter stages of the competition.The World Cup final added another controversial alteration to the traditional match format. A Super Bowl-style half-time show extended the interval to 27 minutes, exceeding the 15-minute maximum stipulated by the Laws of the Game.Foster has played more than 550 professional matches for club and country, and he believes the physical impact of the stoppages could become particularly noticeable for older players because they have less time to remain loose and ready to resume at full intensity.Speaking exclusively on talkSPORT Drive, Foster said: "If you’re an older player it does, if you’re about 32 onwards [it will affect you]."I would like to think they have bikes in the changing room because they will have to get moving pretty quick, because you can stiffen up so quickly."But his concern goes beyond the physical effects. Foster believes the regular interruptions fundamentally alter how teams experience and manage a football match."The halves are not even 45 minutes anymore, they’re quarters. It would not surprise me if these hydration breaks crept into the Premier League," he said."It would not surprise me one little bit. Where there’s money to be made, there’s a way. They will find a reason to justify it." The league has confirmed That prediction is not currently reflected in the Premier League's rules for the new season.World Cup’s Most-Hated Hydration Breaks Could Be ‘Soft-Launched’ in the Champions Leaguethat mandatory hydration breaks will not be introduced across matches in 2026-27. Cooling breaks can still be used when temperatures exceed 30°C (86°F), with the referee deciding before kick-off whether conditions warrant one.Foster is nevertheless concerned that the absence of mandatory breaks in England will not necessarily stop the idea from spreading elsewhere, particularly if football discovers a financial incentive to make the interruptions part of the matchday product.He pointed to VAR as an example of how difficult it can become to reverse a change once football has invested heavily in it, regardless of how supporters feel about the system."There’s nothing we can do as football fans to stop it, they introduced VAR and every single one of us hates it," Foster said."I could do away with VAR tomorrow, but they won’t now because they invested so much money into it."He believes the Champions League could be where the concept is introduced gradually before becoming more widespread."They will do a soft launch in the Champions League, for example, you watch. Clubs will say ‘oh we get an extra million quid'."Foster also believes the World Cup breaks have already changed the way some teams approach their matches, with coaches and players able to treat each interruption almost like a reset point."Teams have been approaching games differently because it’s in quarters, so you can break it down into the four parts. But I hate it."His concerns echo those voiced by other figures in the game. England manager Thomas Tuchel has previously said the stoppages "interrupt and change the identity of a football match", while UEFA has ruled out introducing the same mandatory system in European competition.For now, then, Foster's prediction remains just that: a warning about where he believes football could be heading. The Premier League has specifically rejected mandatory hydration breaks, but his broader concern is that once a change creates a commercial opportunity, football's authorities may eventually find a reason to make it permanent.
Article Summary: Ben Foster fears World Cup hydration breaks could eventually be trialled in the Champions League. Former England goalkeeper fears that what began as a tournament measure could eventually become part of the regular club football landscape. Foster believes the regular interruptions fundamentally alter how teams experience and manage a football match. The Premier League has confirmed that it will introduce mandatory, blanket hydration break among its rule changes for the 2026-27 season.

Article Title: Free hits in Tests can fix no-ball issue: India coach
Article Text:
2nd Test: India's spin attack delivers 10 no-balls against Sri Lanka, third-highest in Tests since 2021

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India's spin bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule proposed introducing free hits in Test cricket, in half-jest, to tackle the problem of bowling no-balls after India's spinners delivered 10 no-balls in the ongoing second Test against Sri Lanka at Sinhalese Sports Club in Colombo."I am no guardian of the rules but if a free-hit comes, obviously, no-balls will definitely be reduced. No team would want to bowl those no-balls and give that extra ball and give those extra runs," said Bahutule after the fourth day's play on Wednesday.India's 10 no-balls were the most bowled by a spin attack since 2021, with Afghanistan heading the list with 14.Bahutule said the issue was being addressed within the team. "Obviously, the take-off point is talked about. They understand what is happening and definitely a process will be put forward in terms of minimising," he said.Bahutule admitted overstepping was an issue that often occurred when bowlers pushed for wickets, and said remedial work continued during India's practice sessions."It is something which we have been working on. It is definitely a concern at times. But when the bowler is putting in that effort and tries to get a wicket in situations where wickets have not been coming, he has a tendency to push himself, but that is not an excuse. A lot of work though has been put in with (Ravindra) Jadeja, with Saransh (Jain), about where the take-off point is and where it should be. But sometimes, the effort they put in for that particular delivery is a bit more and they tend to overstep. I'm sure they will rectify it and get better," the India spin bowling coach asserted.
Article Summary: Sairaj Bahutule proposes introducing free hits in Test cricket. India's spinners delivered 10 no-balls in the ongoing second Test against Sri Lanka. It was the most bowled by a spin attack since 2021, with Afghanistan heading the list with 14.

Brief scores: North Zone 251 & 222 bt West Zone 187 & 234 (overnight 220/7) all out in 57.3 overs (Abid Mushtaq 4/60, Nishant Sindhu 2/59). Semifinals lineup: North vs South; East vs Central

Bengaluru: With West Zone needing 67 runs and North Zone three wickets away from victory, both teams began the fourth and final day of their Duleep Trophy quarterfinal with a win in sight on Wednesday. North were banking on their spinners, while West hoped their capable tailenders, including Shardul Thakur, could help Urvil Patel pull off an unlikely escape at the BCCI Centre of Excellence here.But it took North just 28 minutes to wrap up West, adding only 14 runs to their overnight total of 220 and securing a semifinal date with South Zone, starting Aug 30.Jammu & Kashmir left-arm spinner Abid Mushtaq, who finished with a match haul of nine wickets, uprooted Tanush Kotian's middle stump in the second over to set the wheels in motion. Bowling with accuracy and a flatter trajectory, Abid then had Tushar Deshpande caught sharply at first slip by Abdul Samad.Fellow spinner Nishant Sindhu trapped Urvil leg before wicket to bring the match to an end. Shardul, who walked in at No. 11, did not even face a ball.West had lost the plot late on Tuesday, collapsing from 209/3 to 234 all out as they lost four wickets for 25 runs. Before the late collapse, North Zone left-arm seamer Arshdeep Singh was already looking forward to returning to Punjab. "I was thinking about 'Sher-e-Punjab', going back home, and what time ticket should I book!" said Arshdeep, who claimed four wickets in the match.
Article Summary: North Zone beat West Zone by three wickets in Duleep Trophy quarterfinal. North set up semifinal against South Zone, starting Aug 30. West Zone lost four wickets for 25 runs late on Tuesday, collapsing from 209/3 to 234 all out.

Article Title: Asian Games: Questions over selections across squads
Article Text:
Protistha Samanta competes on the floor exercise during the women's team final and individual qualification of Artistic Gymnastics at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, Scotland, Saturday, July 25, 2026. (AP Photo)

NEW DELHI: India's Asian Games squads are facing fresh selection scrutiny with questions being raised over the criteria used in gymnastics, kurash and karate.In gymnastics, Pranati Nayak is the lone athlete to be cleared. There is no explanation on why other gymnasts who earned nominative, by-name quotas from the Asian Gymnastics Union (AGU) were not considered.Following the 2026 Asian Championships, Nishka Agarwal earned a nominative all-around qualification while Pranati and Protistha Samanta secured nominative qualification as vault specialists. The 2025 Asian meet adds context - Pranati won bronze while Protishta finished fourth.The 2026 championships, held after June 20, fell outside the ministry's qualification window. But if the 2025 Asian event was used as criteria, then Protishta, too, should have made the cut.Protishta had India's best gymnastics result at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games, finishing seventh and becoming the only Indian gymnast to reach the final. Pranati competed there injured and could not make the final cut. "The question is whether the framework was applied consistently for the Asian Games.If yes, then on that basis, Protishta and Nishka, along with men's gymnasts Tapan Mohanty and Yogeshwar Singh, also deserved consideration," said federation sources.Kurash raises another question. India returned from the Hangzhou Games without a medal, yet a six-member team has been cleared after an initial decision by authorities not to send one. With no performance benchmark cited, the selection remains unclear.Karate is equally perplexing. SAI had formed a committee and initially decided not to send a team, according to sources. Yet Alisha Choudhary and Chetan Bhatt have been named. The IOA barred the Karate India Organisation (KIO) from functioning as an NSF over unauthorised selection and otherviolations.Dressage rider Shruti Vora has written to IOA president PT Usha seeking urgent intervention in securing the crucial horse-owner accreditation and blaming the Equestrian Federation of India (EFI) for oversight.
Article Summary: Questions being raised over the criteria used in gymnastics, kurash and karate. Pranati Nayak is the lone athlete to be cleared. There is no explanation on why other gymnasts who earned nominative, by-name quotas from the Asian Gymnastics Union were not considered.

Article Title: Dressage rider Shruti Vora seeks IOA intervention over alleged EFI lapse in horse owner accreditation for Asian Games
Article Text:
Shruti Vora

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Indian dressage rider Shruti Vora has sought the immediate intervention of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA), alleging that the Equestrian Federation of India (EFI) failed to process horse owner accreditation for the Asian Games despite receiving the required documents nearly two months before the deadline.In a letter addressed to the IOA, a copy of which is with TOI, Shruti, a member of the Indian dressage team for the Asian Games, alleged that all required horse owner details, duly notarised, were submitted to the EFI on June 3. According to her, neither she nor fellow athletes received an acknowledgement or response from the federation despite repeated follow-ups on July 13, 17, 19 and 30.Shruti has alleged that the EFI raised the issue with the Asian Games Organising Committee in Japan only on July 29 — nearly two months after receiving the documentation from the athletes. Further reminders were sent by athletes on August 2 and 3, she said.The matter, according to Shruti's letter, took a more serious turn on August 14, when the Asian Games Organising Committee informed the EFI that while FEI regulations permit two horse owner accreditations or passes per horse, the names of the horse owners were required to have been submitted along with the Definite Entries.Shruti has alleged that the delay by the EFI has consequently left horse owners at risk of being denied accreditation, despite the athletes having submitted the required information well in advance."This is not an unavoidable administrative issue," Shruti alleged in her communication to the IOA, describing the situation as a consequence of what she termed a "serious failure" by the federation to act on documentation submitted in time.The dressage rider also questioned whether athletes' interests and essential administrative requirements were being handled with the seriousness expected of a national sports federation representing India at the Asian Games.For equestrian athletes, horse owners and support personnel can play an important role during major international competitions, and Shruti argued that athletes should not be made to bear the consequences of an administrative delay when they had completed the required formalities within the stipulated time.Shruti has now requested the IOA to intervene with the EFI and the Asian Games Organising Committee and ensure that the horse owner accreditations are processed as originally requested.She has also sought written confirmation of the resolution, stressing that the matter is "urgent and time sensitive" with the Games approaching.The rider said repeated attempts by athletes to resolve the matter directly with the EFI had allegedly resulted in neither timely action nor meaningful communication, prompting them to seek IOA intervention.Shruti's letter is an allegation from the athlete's side, and the claims regarding the EFI's handling of the accreditation process have not been independently established. The EFI's response to the allegations was not included in the communication shared by Shruti.The Asian Games 2026 are scheduled to be held in Japan, with the Indian equestrian contingent preparing for the continental multi-sport event. Shruti has urged the IOA to ensure that athletes are not prejudiced by what she alleges are administrative failures beyond their control.
Article Summary: Dressage rider Shruti Vora alleges that the Equestrian Federation of India failed to process horse owner accreditation for the Asian Games. Vora claims that all required horse owner details, duly notarised, were submitted to the EFI on June 3. She alleges that neither she nor fellow athletes received an acknowledgement or response from the federation despite repeated follow-ups.

Article Title: 'Big shock for all of us': Savita Punia urges Hockey India to keep league alive as Women’s HIL faces uncertain future
Article Text:
Savita Punia

KOLKATA: Despite the good showing by the Indian women’s hockey team at the ongoing World Cup, the players were in for a rude shock when they learnt about the concerns surrounding the next edition of the Women’s Hockey India League.Reacting to the news, former India captain and one of the highest-capped player, Savita Punia, told TOI on Wednesday, “Ever since we came to know that teams in the women’s league are considering pulling out, it has definitely been a big shock for all of us. We had been looking forward to the league because we felt it would give us good exposure, especially our young players.”Of the four teams that competed last year, two are considering pulling out while another remains undecided. SG Pipers won the tournament last year, while Shrachi Bengal Tigers clinched the title the year before.“Financially, the league definitely helps, but more importantly, it gives you a platform to train and share your experiences with some of the best players in the world,” added Savita. “There are so many players who dream of doing something for India in hockey, and HIL is one of the best platforms to help them achieve that.”According to one franchise owner, whose team incurred losses running into crores over the two seasons, the biggest reason for considering a pullout was Hockey India’s failure to raise funds as promised.“The tournament isn’t financially viable and that is the only reason for deciding to pull out,” said the owner, who has teams in both the men’s and women’s tournaments.Another franchise official, however, played down those concerns, pointing out that with franchise fees being scrapped from the next edition onwards, and each owner required to pay only Rs 1 crore each for a men’s and women’s team, two teams can now be run at a minimum cost of around Rs 12.5 crore.“Considering that this is only a two-year-old tournament, this should not be a major concern,” the franchise official said.It is understood that Hockey India president Dilip Tirkey, who did not travel to the World Cup unlike several other HI officials, is making efforts to ensure that the tournament goes ahead as planned. He also held meetings with various stakeholders to address the concerns surrounding the league.There had also been discussions about appointing a dedicated sponsorship professional for the HIL, effectively in the role of a director, to drive revenue and commercial partnerships. However, the proposal is understood to have run into differences over remuneration and the reporting structure.While the franchises and Hockey India continue to work through the financial and structural concerns, the players are hoping that a solution is found soon, given the league’s importance to the growth of women’s hockey in the country.“The Indian women’s team is working very hard to take Indian hockey forward, and the HIL is a very big supporter of that journey. So, on behalf of all of us and the women’s team, I would request that the HIL should continue,” Savita further added.With the next edition still facing uncertainty, the coming weeks could prove crucial for the future of the women’s HIL and the opportunities it provides to India’s emerging players.
Article Summary: Women's Hockey India League facing financial and structural concerns. Two teams are considering pulling out while another remains undecided. SG Pipers won the tournament last year, while Shrachi Bengal Tigers clinched the title the year before. Hockey India president Dilip Tirkey is making efforts to ensure that the tournament goes ahead as planned.

Pakistan’s women’s cricket team have taken an unusual route to prepare for the Women’s Asia Cup, playing full T20 matches against a men’s side during their training camp in Lahore.The matches against the Abdul Qadir Cricket Academy featured both teenage and senior male players.Unlike regular practice sessions, the games were played under full Twenty20 rules, with Pakistan aiming to expose their players to greater pressure and improve their decision-making in difficult situations.Pakistan have never won the Women’s Asia Cup. Their best performances came in 2012 and 2016, when they reached the final but lost to India on both occasions. Fatima was among their standout performers, scoring an unbeaten 55 against South Africa and taking 11 wickets, the second-highest tally in the tournament.The captain said dealing with pressure was a major focus during the team’s preparations.“We needed to understand how to handle the pressure better, and that is something which is highlighted whenever there is a big tournament,” she said. “These matches have helped us on that front, and the difference will be visible.“It is very important to stay calm in pressure situations rather than pressing the panic button. We have told the girls to stay calm in the crunch moments, stay in control, trust their hard work and execute the plans.”Fatima will return for the Asia Cup after missing Pakistan’s recent Sri Lanka series while playing in The Hundred.Pakistan are in Group A with India, Thailand and Hong Kong. Sri Lanka batter Sonal Dinusha emerged as one of the biggest positives from the drawn two-Test series against India, producing a remarkable display of resilience and consistency to thwart the visitors’ hopes of a series clean sweep.Dinusha scored three centuries across his four innings in the series, finishing as the leading run-scorer with 420 runs at an average of 140.00. Article Title: ‘Absolutely ridiculous’: Marizanne Kapp slams Cricket Australia’s decision on Anaya Bangar
Article Text:
Marizanne Kapp and Anaya Bangar

CA clears pathway for Anaya to return to competitive cricket

Anaya: ‘Eligibility is not selection’

NEW DELHI: South Africa all-rounder Marizanne Kapp has strongly criticised Cricket Australia’s decision to offer transgender cricketer Anaya Bangar a pathway back into competitive women’s cricket, calling the development “absolutely ridiculous” and saying it “should not be allowed”.Kapp’s reaction came after Australian media reported that Cricket Australia (CA) had cleared Anaya, the daughter of former India cricketer and coach Sanjay Bangar, to return to competitive cricket under its Inclusion of Transgender and Gender Diverse Players in Elite Cricket Policy. The decision has since become a major talking point in the cricketing world.Sharing a report on her Instagram, Kapp wrote: “Absolutely ridiculous. This should not be allowed.”Anaya underwent gender-affirming surgery in March this year and has now been given a pathway towards elite women’s cricket in Australia. Under CA’s decision, she can play community cricket in any state or territory of Australia until March 2027.From March 2027, Anaya can become eligible for elite-level women’s cricket if she continues to meet the policy requirements, including the stipulated testosterone threshold.An expert panel comprising CA’s Head of Integrity Jacqui Partridge, Integrity Partner and Legal representative Emily Yates, Head of Scheduling, Operations and Domestic Cricket Peter Roach, Anti-Doping Medical Officer Dr Peter Harcourt and Team Doctor Dr Pip Inge considered Anaya’s case before confirming the pathway.“Under Cricket Australia's Policy, a player seeking to participate in the female category of Elite Cricket must establish that their serum testosterone concentration has been below 10 nmol/L continuously for a period of no less than 12 months,” CA said in an email to Anaya.The governing body added that, based on the medical information submitted, the requirement would be satisfied in March 2027. Her eligibility from that point will remain conditional on a blood test confirming that her testosterone level remains below 10 nmol/L and that she continues to meet the policy’s requirements.Anaya said the process was neither “automatic or informal” and that CA had considered her medical and surgical history, hormone and testosterone levels, cricketing background, playing footage and scientific and athletic performance work conducted with Manchester Metropolitan University’s Institute of Sport.She also revealed that her most recent blood test in July recorded total testosterone at 0.6 nanomoles, which she said was within the female reference range reported by the laboratory.For Anaya, however, the CA decision represents an opportunity rather than a guarantee of a place in elite cricket.“I want to make another point very clearly. Eligibility is not selection. Cricket Australia has given me a pathway, which does not mean that I have been given a place in a team. I still have to train, compete, perform and earn that opportunity,” she said.“I don't expect my history or my identity to earn me a place on a cricket team. I want my cricket to earn me a place on a cricket team,” she added.Anaya acknowledged the high standard of women’s cricket and the legitimate debate surrounding fairness and competitive integrity in women’s sport, but argued that inclusion and fairness need not be mutually exclusive.“This is why I respect the process Cricket Australia has followed in considering my case,” she said, adding that one of the most difficult possibilities she had faced after transitioning was that cricket might no longer have a place for her.She said she had spent years trying to find a way back and that CA’s decision had finally given her “a pathway to try”.Anaya’s pathway could eventually include an opportunity to pursue the Women’s Big Bash League, provided she meets the eligibility requirements in March 2027.
Article Summary: South Africa all-rounder Marizanne Kapp has strongly criticised Cricket Australia's decision to offer transgender cricketer Anaya Bangar a pathway back into competitive women's cricket. Kapp called the development “absolutely ridiculous” and said it “should not be allowed” Anaya underwent gender-affirming surgery in March this year and has now been given a pathway towards elite women’s cricket in Australia.

Article Title: In 1936, Cotar Ramaswami became only second Indian to make Test debut after turning 40; he also played at Wimbledon, disappeared from his home in 1985 and remains listed as ‘death unknown’

Seated: Phiroze Edulji Palia, Cottari Kanakaiya Nayudu, Maharaj Kumar of Vizianagram, Mohammad Nissar, Vijay Merchant. (Photo/Getty Images)

From player to manager and selector

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The disappearance

Only 13 cricketers in the history of Test cricket have made their debuts after turning 40. Two of them were Indians — Rustomji Jamshedji Dorabji Jamshedji and Cotar Ramaswami Jamshedji remains the oldest Indian to make his Test debut. He was 41 years and 27 days old when he played against England in Mumbai on December 15, 1933. Ramaswami, born on June 16, 1896, in Madras (now Chennai), made his Test debut aged 40 years and 39 days against England at Manchester on July 25, 1936.Born on November 18, 1892, in Bombay (now Mumbai), Jamshedji played only one Test for India, while Ramaswami played two.But Ramaswami's story goes beyond his short Test career. He played First-Class cricket for 27 years, represented Cambridge University in tennis and even appeared at Wimbledon. Decades later, he left his home in Chennai one morning and was never seen or heard from again.Cotar Ramaswami was the youngest son of Buchi Babu Naidu, who was a trailblazer in Madras cricket.Ramaswami was a left-handed batter and played 53 First-Class matches, scoring 2,400 runs at 28.91, including two centuries. He also took 30 wickets at 33.06.He came from a family closely connected to cricket. His brothers M Baliah and M Venkataramanjulu played First-Class cricket, as did his son C Ramaswaroop.Four of his nephews and a grand-nephew also played First-Class cricket.Ramaswami made his First-Class debut for Indians against the Europeans in 1915-16. He scored 21 and 31 and took two wickets for 24 runs in the first innings.The following season, in the same fixture, he scored 92 and 44 and took six wickets for 126 runs in the match.The performances caught the attention of the Madras cricket fraternity. However, opportunities were limited. Ramaswami was generally playing only one First-Class match a year and had made just four appearances before leaving for Cambridge in 1919.At Cambridge, Ramaswami continued playing cricket but also took up tennis.He studied there until 1923 and represented Cambridge University in men's doubles. After winning matches during a tour of the Netherlands, he was selected for the Davis Cup team.That year, he also played at Wimbledon.Ramaswami won his first-round match against Britain's Ulysses Williams in a five-set contest, 5-7, 8-10, 6-0, 14-12, 6-3.He was then beaten by Nicolae Misu, who won 6-1, 6-4, 6-3.After completing his studies at Cambridge, Ramaswami returned to India and joined the Agricultural Department as an officer.He continued playing cricket for Madras and was part of the first Ranji Trophy match against Mysore, scoring 26.In 1936, at the age of 40, he was selected for India's tour of England.In his book,, Ramaswami claimed modestly that he was convinced he had been chosen for reasons other than cricket because he had become 'bulky and slow.' His performances on the tour suggested otherwise.He scored 737 runs in First-Class matches at an average of 30.70 before making his Test debut in the second Test at Old Trafford.At 40 years and 37 days, he became the second-oldest Indian to make his Test debut when he received the India cap in the second Test match of the series, at Old Trafford.He scored 40 and 60 in the match, helping India draw the Test. It was also the match in which Vijay Merchant and Mushtaq Ali put together their famous opening partnership of 203 runs.Ramaswami followed that with scores of 29 and 41 not out in the final Test at The Oval.He finished his Test career with 170 runs at an average of 56.66. That was the end of his international career, but Ramaswami continued playing for Madras for several more years.His First-Class career lasted 25 years, during which he scored 2,261 runs at 28.26. He was known as a free-stroking left-handed batter, with a strong drive on both sides of the wicket.He also represented the Hindus in the Bombay Quadrangular and Pentangular tournaments.Ramaswami remained involved in cricket after his playing career.He managed India's tour of the West Indies in 1953. The team became one of the most popular Indian sides to visit the Caribbean.In the late 1950s, he became a national selector. The period, however, was marked by disagreements over team selection and India's poor performances.It culminated during the 1958-59 home series against the West Indies, when India had four captains in five Tests and there was considerable disagreement over selection.Ramaswami's story took an unexplained turn decades later. On the morning of October 15, 1985, he left his residence in Adyar and never returned.There have been occasional reports of sightings over the years, but none were confirmed.Wisden eventually listed him as `presumed dead'. His whereabouts were never established, although record books later began listing January 1990 as his date of death.Wisden continues to list his death as "death unknown".His family knew little about what happened to him, apart from the fact that he did not want to become a burden on them.
Article Summary: Cotar Ramaswami was the youngest son of Buchi Babu Naidu, who was a trailblazer in Madras cricket. He played First-Class cricket for 27 years, represented Cambridge University in tennis and even appeared at Wimbledon. Decades later, he left his home in Chennai one morning and was never seen or heard from again.

Article Title: 1139 minutes! How defiant Sonal Dinusha denied India a 2-0 series sweep

TimesofIndia.com in Colombo:

I thought, jeez, this guy can play. I love the way he plays Test cricket. He thinks about it. He plays to his strengths and he is a smart cricketer Garry Kirsten

1139 minutes, 722 balls, 420 runs and three hundreds. Over the last two weeks, Sonal Dinusha accumulated staggering numbers, but the time he spent at the crease will stand the test of time. It was the major reason why Sri Lanka lived to fight on Day 5 in Galle and Colombo against India. Before diving into his heroics, it's important to note his entry points in the four innings against India to add much-needed context.90/4 and 47/4 in the first Test, followed by 122/4 and 209/4 in the second. While the scorecard makes for comfortable reading in the final essay in Colombo, the situation there was the trickiest. Sri Lanka needed to play for time — a lot of it. Two quick wickets in the next few overs meant the 25-year-old was left with just the bowlers for company. He had faced a similar situation in the previous innings, but the stakes were highest on Days 4 and 5 at the SSC, with India desperate for the remaining wickets to enforce a result.Dinusha came with a plan and stuck to it. He made time his closest ally. The support from the other end, coupled with tactical brilliance, meant India toiled for over 86 overs but still couldn't get the result they wanted.He consumed time, scored runs and literally swept India out of the contest on the final day of the Test. The sweep and reverse-sweep were his two strongest shots in the innings that preceded the fourth-innings masterclass, but he looked in maximum control when it mattered most.Shubman Gill was aware of the sweep challenge and covered that region with constant protection for the hit on both sides of the wicket. But it was Dinusha's smart use of footwork that left the visitors clueless throughout the day. Over 40% of his runs in the series came off sweeps, but his control stood out in Colombo. With no vicious bite from the surface and LBW and bowled becoming the least expected modes of dismissal, Dinusha feasted and became only the third batter ever to score twin hundreds in a match where his team was asked to follow on.Doing it from No.6, with the tail for company, he also became the fifth overall batter to achieve the rare feat.Dinusha's compact game, approach against both spin and pace, and stubbornness made his time against the Indian bowlers difficult throughout the series, establishing him as the best batter across both teams. The number of overs he spent batting with the tail should become an ideal template for batters operating from No.6 and below in the format, which is why his effort attracted plenty of praise from the opposition camp too."He (Dinusha) played really well, his defense was solid, he played some really good sweep shots. And in this match, I don't think there was even a half-chance that he went to a fielder," Gill said while praising the thorn in their flesh."We thought we can get him with pace but there wasn't enough of it on the wicket. Someone like Prasidh was consistently bowling 135-140kmph and bowling bouncers but he was able to defend. So we could see there wasn't enough pace in the wicket to challenge him again and again," he further added.Gill's comments carried an undertone of helplessness, which remained the order of the day before early handshakes brought the curtains down on India's hopes of returning with a 2-0 scoreline. Add to this the frustration of not being able to wrap up the tail quickly in either innings. Over 44 overs in the first innings and then another 90-plus in the second, Dinusha ensured India remained on the park longer than they would have liked. This storyline has continued, with minor adjustments, since Galle."I think it's never easy batting at six in a team because often you come in under pressure. I saw that he really thrives in tough situations. The first time I watched him bat properly was in the first innings in the West Indies," Gary Kirsten said in the post-match press conference."He came in at seven and we were 110 for five and he put on a 100 with the captain (Dhananjaya de Silva)."I thought, jeez, this guy can play. I love the way he plays Test cricket. He thinks about it. He plays to his strengths and he is a smart cricketer," added the veteran coach.There were early butterflies and nervousness in his movements in Galle, but Colombo tasted like different gravy as he gave nothing away and carried the team along in a manner only he could have. In Gill's words, he didn't give a "half a chance", while coach Kirsten quickly termed it one of the "great saves of Sri Lankan Test cricket".The approach remained uncomplicated, allowing him to become only the second batter to have four consecutive scores of 80+; Simon Katich from Australia is the only other batter to achieve the feat, back in 2017. And when he hit Gill's first delivery for a six with the handshake formalities impending, the left-hander could well have murmured to himself — 'keep bowling, I am seeing it like a football now'. He indeed was sighting it better than any other batter, and it wasn't a surprise that he walked away unbeaten, unconquered and the biggest pain for Gill & Co.
Article Summary: Sonal Dinusha is only the third batter ever to score twin hundreds in a match where his team was asked to follow on. Dinusha's compact game, approach against both spin and pace, and stubbornness made his time against the Indian bowlers difficult throughout the series.

Article Title: ‘It takes only one moment of foolishness to lose a Test’: Ashwin’s blunt warning to Rishabh Pant
Article Text:
India's Rishabh Pant plays a shot (PTI Photo)

Ashwin rejects ‘once-in-a-generation’ argument

Ashwin urges Pant to put team needs ahead of attacking instincts

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Ravichandran Ashwin believes Rishabh Pant needs to show greater awareness of match situations and take more responsibility with the bat, despite the wicketkeeper-batter putting together a respectable series against Sri Lanka.Pant finished the two-Test series with 168 runs and two half-centuries. However, Ashwin feels the numbers do not tell the complete story and wants the India batter to exercise more judgement when deciding how to attack.Pant's aggressive approach has come under scrutiny over the past few months, with questions being raised about whether he sometimes takes unnecessary risks and fails to put enough value on his wicket.The former India spinner pointed to Pant's dismissal against South Africa in Guwahati last year as an example. While captaining India in the absence of Shubman Gill, Pant charged down the track against Marco Jansen and edged the delivery to the wicketkeeper.Pant is currently a Test-only player for India after falling out of favour in the white-ball formats. Ashwin believes his decision-making in Test cricket remains an area that needs attention.“My expectation from Rishabh Pant hasn't been fulfilled till now. I am very sorry. Sonal Dinusha had his strike rate up there. But the difference is high-risk options. When you have the game in your hand, these are all statements: ‘That’s how Rishabh plays.' It is about what your team needs,” Ashwin said on ‘Ash Ki Baat’.During the discussion, the host argued that Pant's unique ability and his history of producing match-winning performances meant he should be given some freedom to play his natural game.Ashwin, however, insisted that even an exceptional player cannot be exempt from the demands of the situation.“Rishabh played a class knock in Sydney and Brisbane, but you couldn't have won that match without Washington Sundar and Shardul Thakur. It takes 11 cricketers to build a Test and win it in the last session of the game, but it takes only 1 moment of foolishness to lose a Test,” said Ashwin.The former off-spinner clarified that his criticism was not directed at Pant's attacking style itself. Instead, he wants the batter to recognise when the situation demands a different approach.“I am just talking about the times when these chances are being taken when the game is on the line. I love Rishabh the player. It is about playing situations in this format. Sehwag and Gilchrist played high brand of cricket, but these two don't get edged out while dancing down to Marco Jansen when your team is trailing by 500 runs. Don't place these marketing lines in front of me ever again,” he added.Ashwin also called for more straightforward feedback for Pant, arguing that his status as a special talent should not shield him from criticism.The former India spinner pointed out that Pant has now played 50 Tests and believes his experience means he should be expected to take greater responsibility.“Don't give one player special treatment. This once-in-a-generation player backing, then give it to everyone. Jaiswal is also such a player. All I'm saying, Rishabh, is that he is experienced; he has played 50 Tests. He needs to take responsibility. Don't come up with this ‘once-in-a-generation’ argument. It is because of his decision-making that he's not playing the other two formats. The day you tell him the truth, he will be an all-format player for India,” said Ashwin.Pant's current status outside India's ODI and T20I squads has added further significance to Ashwin's comments. While he remains a key part of India's Test setup, Ashwin believes adapting his approach to different match situations could be the key to Pant eventually returning as an all-format player.
Article Summary: Ravichandran Ashwin believes Rishabh Pant needs to show greater awareness of match situations. The wicketkeeper-batter put together a respectable series against Sri Lanka. Ashwin feels the numbers do not tell the complete story and wants Pant to exercise more judgement when deciding how to attack.

Article Title: ‘Got to learn from the opposition as well’: Shubman Gill reflects after Sri Lanka deny India clean sweep
Article Text:
India's Captain Shubman Gill, left, on day five of second Test (PTI Photo)

Gill praises Padikkal 's impact

Gill identifies Suthar as future spin leader

Dinusha leads Sri Lanka's fightback

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India captain Shubman Gill admitted there were plenty of lessons for his side despite the disappointment of missing out on a series clean sweep against Sri Lanka, while backing the team to respond strongly when they travel to New Zealand later this year.India had to settle for a draw in the second Test at Colombo after Sri Lanka's lower order produced a determined fightback, led by Sonal Dinusha's unbeaten 133. India still won the two-match series 1-0, but the dropped opportunity to secure another victory affected their World Test Championship points percentage, leaving them fifth in the standings ahead of the New Zealand series beginning on November 19.Speaking in a video by BCCI, Gill said the way Sri Lanka battled over the final three days deserved recognition and felt India could take lessons from their opponents as well."A lot of learnings in this series. I think we played decently well. Obviously not the result that we wanted in this match. After day two, we hoped that it was going to be a win for us, and then Sri Lanka batting the way that they did for these three days. Sometimes you have got to learn from the opposition as well and give credit to them for the way that they played, and hopefully we have a good series in New Zealand."One of the biggest positives for India was the form of Devdutt Padikkal, who was named Player of the Series after producing two centuries.With Sai Sudharsan unavailable because of injury, Padikkal made the most of his opportunity and strengthened his case for the No. 3 position in India's Test batting order.Gill was particularly impressed by Padikkal's ability to convert good starts into substantial scores."We speak about once a batsman is set, he should make the most of it, and Devdutt showed that. Very positive signs for us, and the way he batted in the series was a treat to watch, you know, truly tells the mindset of a player, and that is a great positive sign for us," said Gill about Paddikal.Padikkal ended the series as India's leading run-scorer, making 328 runs in three innings at an average of 109.33. His tally included two centuries and a highest score of 167.Across his four Tests and six innings so far, Padikkal has accumulated 418 runs at an average of 69.66, with two centuries and one fifty.Gill also singled out Manav Suthar for praise after the left-arm spinner emerged as India's leading wicket-taker in the series.Suthar's standout moment came in the first Test at Galle, where he claimed 10 wickets to register the first ten-wicket haul of his career. Gill believes the spinner has the qualities to become a long-term leader of India's spin attack."He has been magnificent for us, and I think he is going to be someone who is going to be leading the spin attack for India for a very long time. And the way he bowled in this match and even in the first match was a treat to watch. Every time he comes on to bowl, it feels like he is going to create those chances and going to get us wickets, and hopefully he keeps doing that," said the skipper.Suthar finished the two-Test series with 16 wickets at an average of 21.06. His haul included a four-wicket spell and a six-wicket haul in the first Test, while his best innings figures were 6/55.India's first-innings total of 503/9 was built around three-figure knocks from Padikkal and Dhruv Jurel.Padikkal made 117 from 193 balls, hitting 12 fours, while Jurel remained unbeaten on 115 from 177 deliveries, with nine fours and two sixes. Rishabh Pant contributed 63 from 89 balls, including six fours and two sixes, while Gill scored 50 from 108 balls with six fours.Asitha Fernando was Sri Lanka's most successful bowler, finishing with four wickets.Sri Lanka responded with 290 in their first innings. Dinusha again played a central role, scoring 103 from 162 balls with eight fours and three sixes. Pasindu Sooriyabandara added a valuable 80 from 133 balls, striking nine fours.Prasidh Krishna and Suthar claimed three wickets apiece for India.Asked to follow on, Sri Lanka were reduced to 218/6 before Dinusha and Keshara Nuwantha launched a stubborn recovery. The pair added 112 runs, with Nuwantha making 46 from 150 balls, including four boundaries.Dinusha completed another century, remaining unbeaten on 133 from 264 deliveries with eight fours and two sixes. His resistance, combined with a lower-order effort that repeatedly frustrated India's bowlers, carried Sri Lanka to 429/9.The draw ended India's hopes of a 2-0 series victory, but Gill believes the experience can prove valuable when India return to Test action in New Zealand in November.
Article Summary: India had to settle for a draw in the second Test at Colombo after Sri Lanka's lower order produced a determined fightback. India still won the two-match series 1-0, but the dropped opportunity to secure another victory affected their World Test Championship points percentage. Captain Shubman Gill said there were plenty of lessons for his side despite the disappointment of missing out on a series clean sweep.

Article Title: ‘Blatantly trying to kill him’: Imran Khan’s sons make explosive claims over ex-Pakistan PM prison conditions
Article Text:
Imran Khan (AP Photo)

Sons fear for Imran’s health

Interview sparks PCB controversy

Former captains back call for medical care

Sulaiman Khan and Kasim Khan, the sons of former Pakistan captain and Prime Minister Imran Khan, have expressed serious concern over their father’s health and the conditions in which he is being held in prison.Speaking to former England captain and Sky Sports commentator Michael Atherton, the brothers alleged that Imran has been kept in prolonged isolation and has not received adequate medical care. They said they fear for his safety as he approaches three years in prison.Kasim claimed that Imran has suffered a major loss of vision in one eye, estimating that he has lost around 80 per cent of his sight in it. He also said Imran was recently seen wearing an eye patch.According to the brothers, Imran spends more than 23 hours a day alone inside a small cell, with restricted access to books and basic comforts. They also alleged that the cell does not have air conditioning despite the summer heat.“They are not even acting with any kind of strategy any more. It is not very clear what they are doing, just blatantly trying to kill him in there. Keep him in as long as possible, and silence him.The last time he was able to speak to our aunties and anyone else, he said the conditions have severely worsened recently. He has been relating it to other political prisoners who have been killed or who have died in prison. Right now, it is worse than ever, completely isolating him more than 23 hours a day in a cell," Kasim said.Kasim said the priority for the family was now ensuring that Imran receives appropriate medical treatment. He described seeing his father with an eye patch and said the former Pakistan captain appeared visibly stressed.“Right now, it’s really crucial for us that he gets proper treatment. He had an eye patch on for the eye situation, seemed visibly stressed, and that is something that is very hard for us to imagine because he embodies a very calm, assured presence, every time I have ever seen him, including being at gunpoint. A car we were in was robbed, and he was the calmest person there, including the robbers," he added.The brothers also discussed their attempts to travel to Pakistan and visit their father. They claimed their visas had been blocked on technical grounds and said they were willing to accept the possibility of arrest if it gave them an opportunity to see Imran.Sulaiman recalled the family's reaction after Imran was taken for a medical examination following a court order.“We were cautiously optimistic. Our fears were confirmed when, instead of being taken to the private hospital, where he was meant to be taken, he was just taken to a government medical facility for a few hours, and then taken straight back to jail," said Sulaiman.He claimed the examination at the government facility lasted only about an hour and that doctors waiting at Shifa Hospital were not given the opportunity to treat Imran.“In reality, it was an hour check-up by government officials who said, ‘Great, he’s OK’, and then said we will now send him to the independent hospital, Shifa. Instead, they left all the doctors waiting, our auntie waiting, who is a doctor, and sent him straight back to jail," he added.The interview, which was aired during the lunch break of the second Test between England and Pakistan at Lord’s on Thursday, also created an unexpected controversy involving the PCB.The board lodged a formal complaint with Sky Sports over the broadcast. Reports further suggested that the PCB considered asking Pakistan's players not to return to the field after lunch if the interview was shown.The players eventually returned to the field and the Test continued as scheduled.The interview came shortly after renewed international concern over Imran's medical treatment. He had been taken to a government hospital for a medical examination following a court order relating to his treatment.The concerns surrounding Imran have also drawn an appeal from a group of former international captains, including Indian cricket greats Sunil Gavaskar and Kapil Dev.The former captains wrote to Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, urging his government to ensure that Imran receives proper medical treatment and humane conditions while in prison.The appeal was framed as a humanitarian intervention rather than a political statement.Imran remains one of the most prominent figures in Pakistan cricket history. He led the country to its first men's ODI World Cup title in 1992 before entering politics and eventually becoming Pakistan's prime minister.
Article Summary: Sons of former Pakistan captain express concern over their father's health. They say he has been kept in prolonged isolation and has not received adequate medical care. The brothers said they fear for his safety as he approaches three years in prison. The interview was aired during the lunch break of the second Test.

Article Title: The making of Sonal Dinusha: Humble roots and the sweep shot behind Sri Lanka’s new star’s rise
Article Text:
Sonal Dinusha (Getty Images)

A boy with a clear vision

From spinner to batting star

The sweep that became a weapon

Thirteen years of patience

A new chapter

Sonal Dinusha’s twin centuries against India in Galle were the result of much more than a good run of form. The Sri Lankan all-rounder’s remarkable effort in the second Test was built over 13 years of hard work, discipline and the constant backing of a coach who first spotted his potential as a young cricketer.Dinusha scored 103 in Sri Lanka’s first innings and followed it with an unbeaten 133 in the second. His second hundred came after Sri Lanka were forced to follow on, helping them recover from 290 all out and secure a draw and deny India register a 2-0 clean sweep.Dinusha grew up in a humble background without the financial resources needed to pursue cricket easily. But from a young age, he showed a determination to make a career in the sport.At the Colombo Cricket Club, coach Sonal Dulshan Alwalage became an important figure in his development. What started as a coach working with a talented youngster eventually became a 13-year project.Dulshan and people around Dinusha helped him continue training when financial limitations could have forced him away from the game. The young cricketer remained focused on his goal and gradually developed into a player capable of competing at the highest level.Like many young cricketers, Dinusha initially found his identity as a bowler. He developed into an effective left-arm spinner, but over time it became clear that his batting could take him much further. His development was built around adaptability, technique and an understanding of the game. He learned to assess situations quickly rather than simply attack every ball.One of the clearest examples of that development is his sweep shot.The sweep has been one of Dinusha’s most productive strokes, particularly on pitches where spinners play a major role. It is not a shot he discovered after reaching international cricket.He has worked on it since childhood, spending long hours repeating the stroke in the nets. His training sessions could stretch for two to three hours, with the sweep receiving particular attention.That preparation was evident in Galle. Dinusha repeatedly used the shot to counter India’s spinners and turn difficult deliveries into scoring opportunities.Dinusha’s journey to the Sri Lankan team was not sudden. It was built through years of club cricket, training and patience.When his national selection finally arrived, it represented the culmination of more than a decade of work. For Dulshan, who had stayed with him throughout the journey, it was an emotional moment and confirmation that the long-term project had worked.Dinusha also brought leadership experience with him. He became captain of the Colombo Cricket Club, giving him an opportunity to develop his understanding of leading a team.Dinusha is still only at the beginning of his international career. But his performances against India have offered a glimpse of what years of preparation can produce.The twin centuries were not simply two outstanding innings. They were the latest chapter in a journey that began with a young boy, limited resources, a supportive coach and a clear dream.Thirteen years later, that dream has turned into a Test career — and Dinusha now has the opportunity to build much more.
Article Summary: Sonal Dinusha scored twin centuries against India in Galle. Sri Lankan all- rounder's effort was built over 13 years of hard work. Dinusha grew up in a humble background without the financial resources needed to pursue cricket easily. He developed into an effective left-arm spinner, but his batting could take him much further.

Sonal Dinusha finished the two-Test series against India with another century and a new Test record, scoring 176 runs through sweep shots, the most by any batter in a Test series.The 25-year-old left-hander remained unbeaten on 133 in Sri Lanka's second innings as the hosts forced a draw in the second Test at the Sinhalese Sports Club in Colombo on Thursday. India still won the two-match series 1-0 after their victory in Galle.Dinusha's unbeaten 133 came after his first-innings 103 in Colombo and his century in the first Test in Galle. It was his third hundred in four innings in the series.According to Cricinfo, Dinusha scored 176 runs through sweep shots across the series.
